gary: Since Linda passed, the garage is where I feel most like myself.
Hal doesn't like me much, but nobody on this street knows wiring like I do.
Gary's guilt about the speaker and the skipped permits is nagging at me, but Hal and Rosa seem to be letting it slide for now.
Donna has been surprisingly generous with her time and her spare paddle, and I think I'm starting to look forward to our Saturday doubles match.
Donna has been pushing me into pickleball with a grin and a booked court, and I'm surprised how much I'm looking forward to being her doubles partner.
My parade cart still needs its wiring finished, but getting out with Donna today reminded me that a bit of pickleball is worth more than a perfect circuit.
Donna keeps dragging me out of the garage, but I'm glad she won't let me hide behind my soldering iron, and I think I might actually enjoy being her doubles partner.
I've promised to file the Architectural Review form before Saturday, and I want to keep my word so I can stay on the court with Donna at eight.
donna: Partners make or break your ladder ranking, and mine keep moving to Ocala.
Gary has quick hands and nothing to do on weekends. He just doesn't know he wants to play yet.
Gary is surprisingly easy to talk into things, and I'm glad he showed up to the court and kept the ball in play, even if he calls himself terrible.
Rosa's dinner invitation and the doubles partnership with Gary make me feel like this town is starting to feel like a real community again.
Gary is a good sport who needs a little nudging, but I think he'll be a fine doubles partner once he gets the hang of the kitchen line.
I want Saturday at eight to be a real win for Gary and me, so I'm going to book those practice sessions and make sure he has the spare paddle he needs.
Gary and I finally have a plan for Saturday, and I'm looking forward to climbing the doubles ladder with him at my side.
Hal's flamingo rule is a pain, but keeping the street tidy matters to me, and I'd rather settle it with a friendly chat than a violation notice.
hal: Rules exist so neighbors don't have to argue. Somebody has to keep them.
The street was quieter before the new speaker arrived.
Gary's garage wiring worries me, but I also know the rules matter, and I'm not sure how to balance loyalty with what I owe the town.
Rosa's welcome dinner invitation surprised me, and I'm hoping I can sit at her table without turning every conversation into a complaint about flamingos.
I've been logging Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos so carefully that I'm starting to wonder whether I'm keeping the peace or just keeping score on my neighbors.
Rosa's dinner invitation caught me off guard, and I'm hoping a plate of food and some good company might make me less of a rulebook and more of a friend.
Rosa's dinner on Saturday should be a good chance to get to know her better, and I'm glad to have been invited.
Donna and Gary's doubles ladder challenge is going to be a lot of fun to watch, even if I'm not sure I'll keep up with them.
rosa: I moved here to slow down, and so far I've worked four shifts and met nobody.
These three neighbors clearly have history I don't understand yet.
Gary turned a broken disposal into a favor I can't repay, and I think he's the kind of neighbor who shows up without being asked.
Hosting dinner for Gary, Donna, and Hal feels like the right way to thank them and finally make this street feel like home.
Hal's easy yes to my dinner made me happy, and I'm glad the welcome will finally bring Gary, Donna, and Hal together at my table on Saturday.
Planning this dinner around my shifts and the grocery list reminded me that I want to be the kind of neighbor who makes people feel at home on Magnolia Loop.
Hal said he'll come to my welcome dinner and keep the rulebook in his pocket, which made me smile, and I'm glad someone here already feels like a neighbor.
I keep checking the ladder standings and court bookings to find Donna, and I hope a friendly game with her will help us get to know each other.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
